prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Full SCENE STATE SHEET for a physical Mars expedition game. Match the supplied realistic painterly cream-and-teal machinery, ochre landscape, restrained cobalt science equipment, mustard rover fittings. Locally made parts are simple cut straight steel and bolted joints, never elaborate molded industrial machinery. Factory precision parts are imported. No people, text, numerals, labels, captions, borders, arrows, diagrams or UI. Each panel repeats EXACTLY the same camera, framing, object positions, light, room/landscape and perspective, changing ONLY the specified state. Every recurring object is the same actual object. Frame the full installation in the upper two thirds; lower third is quiet natural floor or ground for the movable inventory. No loose decorative objects. Whole scenes will be cropped into registered fixed targets; keep independent working regions clearly separated. Square panels, not portrait strips.
Layout: 2 columns by 2 rows of equal SQUARE scenes. Reading order left to right then next row. An outdoor services bay near the industrial solar area. At right stands ONE compact factory electrolyzer stack on a low plain steel rack. Its electrical and cooling service tails are already attached behind it. At left is the existing cream water processor with a distinct polished-water outlet facing the rack. There is a clear route between outlet and stack water inlet. Only the H2/O2 receivers are missing, never portray two independent electrolysis machines.
STATE 1: Electrolyzer stack positioned and powered/cooled. Its water inlet is capped. No gas manifold or buffer cylinders.
STATE 2: Factory gas-control manifold blocks now fitted on the rack, with two separate gas outlet routes waiting. Water inlet still disconnected. No cylinders.
STATE 3: A service water hose now joins the processor polishing outlet to the electrolyzer water inlet. Same separate gas manifold, no buffer cylinders yet.
STATE 4: Two modest factory buffer cylinders are secured side by side to that rack, each with its own separate keyed gas connection, one hydrogen and one oxygen. No mixing junction. Existing power, cooling and water stay attached.
